title: The bunkbed conjecture for transitive tournaments
scope: For every n and all u,v : Fin n, the number of outcomes on the n*n tokens of the transitive tournament T_n bunkbed in which (u,false) reaches (v,true) is at most the number in which it reaches (v,false). One independent fair horizontal token per arc per layer, one shared bidirectional vertical token per index, reachability as reflexive transitive closure, fixed endpoints.
source_targets: European Journal of Combinatorics 128 (2025) 104188, model D7
validation: Thirty-three modules compiled and kernel-checked from an empty build twice: in the assembly lane and, from a sealed archive, in the independent review. Reviewer read all modules; transitive closure of 6913 constants has only the three permitted axioms and no unsafe or partial constant; Lean controls at n=1 and n=2; statement fidelity PASS against the source and the literal. Root verified receipts, hashes and the mathlib pin.
substantive_reason: Resolves the exact infinite family posed by Hollom as Conjecture 6.4, in the correct model, after the statement was shown to fail for general acyclic digraphs. It is not a scope, domain or endpoint repair. The source calls the case more difficult than expected and says complete-graph methods lack the needed symmetries. The proof finds the exact sufficient statistic that completeness of the order provides.
contrary_scope_assessment: The proof is short and elementary and uses an old reflection idea; E7 is an instance of an immediately derived column-homogeneous extension, which carries no separate credit. No complete applicable prior-to-target bridge was found despite direct attempts through injections, the van Hintum-Lammers and Leander arguments and the Przybylowski paper. Significance is recorded as modest.
novelty_standard: Qualified bounded source-primary investigation, not worldwide priority certification.
prior_limits: The final journal version of Przybylowski, DOI 10.1016/j.ejc.2025.104289, is closed and unread; the supplied arXiv v2 is not final-equivalence evidence. Registry roots closed. Four searches in total across two reviews found no proof or disproof.
process_adjudication: Disclosed and judged non-substantive: the second qualification read the raw line after the author proposal; the assembly lane ran verify_frozen once without its argument and one read-only one-liner outside its runner; the independent reviewer ran display filters and one scratchpad edit outside its runner; earlier Pi lanes inspected signatures before first writes. Certificate content rests on fresh replay and independent audit rather than on those histories.
trust_limits: Upstream Lean, mathlib and their oleans are trusted through pins and were not rebuilt. Reviewers are AI systems, not human referees. The relabeling of an abstract transitive tournament to Fin n is not formalized and is trivial.
paper_corrections: Root corrected Remark 4.1 and status text only; see qa/ROOT-CORRECTIONS.json. The main proof was not changed.
not_claimed: Separate credit for the column-homogeneous extension
Any statement for general acyclic digraphs
